memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From there he went on toward the hills east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to the Lord and called on the name of the Lord. - Gen 12:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the pattern of Abram's life: a tent and an altar. The tent speaks of his pilgrim status - he was a stranger passing through, holding this world lightly. The altar speaks of his worship - wherever he went, he built a place to meet with God. Temporary dwelling, permanent worship.

Wherever Abram pitched his tent, he built an altar. Worship was not something he did occasionally, in special places; it travelled with him. He "called on the name of the Lord" - the same phrase used of Seth's godly line back in Genesis 4:26. Abram belonged to the people who call on God.

This is a searching picture for us. What do we build permanently, and what do we hold loosely? Many of us reverse Abram's pattern - we build permanent houses and pitch temporary altars, investing everything in what won't last and squeezing God into the margins.

Hebrews says Abram "lived in tents... looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God" (Heb 11:9-10). He held earthly things loosely because his real hope was elsewhere. Let that shape your life: hold your possessions and plans like a tent, and make your worship the thing you build wherever you go. Call on the name of the Lord - He is worth more than any address.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you building permanence into things that won't last?
- Does your worship travel with you wherever you go?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me hold this world loosely like a tent, and build my worship of You wherever I go. Let my hope rest in the city You are building, not in what I can build here.
Amen.
